faqs.q: How long does SEO take to work in Croatia?
faqs.a: For Croatian-language local keywords, most businesses see movement in 2 to 3 months because competition is thinner than in English markets. Tourist-season keywords need to be built well before summer; starting in winter for a summer season is the smart timing.

faqs.q: Should my site be in Croatian or English?
faqs.a: Both, for different jobs. Croatian for local customers and year-round services, English (plus German or Italian where it pays) for tourism-facing pages. I use hreflang so the versions help rather than compete with each other.

faqs.q: Is SEO worth it for a seasonal coastal business?
faqs.a: Yes, because the season is short and the competition for it is fierce. Ranking before June decides your whole summer. The businesses that win are the ones whose pages were ready in March, not the ones scrambling in July.

faqs.q: Can you help a Zagreb B2B company, not just tourism?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Zagreb's B2B market searches in Croatian during working hours, and most competitors have weak sites. Service pages in natural Croatian plus a complete Business Profile usually move the needle fast.

faqs.q: How much does SEO cost for a Croatian business?
faqs.a: It depends on whether you need one language or four, and whether you are fighting for Zagreb local terms or international tourism keywords. After a free audit I quote a fixed monthly scope, so you always know what you are paying for.
